program.program_name: Airline and Flight Operations Commercial Pilot (Rotary-Wing)

offerings.status: Refer to official BCIT program page

courses.course_name: Introduction to Airport and Airside Operations
courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: This course will provide a solid foundation of the essential role the air transport system plays in Canada and the United States. Topics include regulatory requirements, operational processes and management practices within the airport sector. Evaluation includes exams, airport report and online discussions. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.course_name: Occupational Health and Safety in Aviation
courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: ​This introductory course in occupational health and safety equips students with the foundational knowledge required to work safely within an aviation environment. Learners will examine key regulatory frameworks, including the Canada Labour Code Part II, Canadian Occupational Health and Safety Regulations, Aviation Occupational Health and Safety Regulations, and the Workers Compensation Act administered by WorkSafeBC. The course also addresses critical workplace topics, including fire safety, aviation-specific hazards and risk management, workplace drug and alcohol use policies, and the use of personal protective equipment (PPE). In addition, students will complete WorkSafeBC Basic First Aid and WHMIS training as part of the course. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: This course will introduce participants to Safety Management Systems (SMS) as required by Transport Canada and the impact it has on the aviation industry. Students will learn a systematic approach and evolution of safety management in aviation. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: ​This course will provide a broad understanding of all aspects of the airline industry within Canada and globally. It will cover the regulatory compliance for both Canadian and International airlines, the structure of the airline industry, airline economics, strategy, structure, technology, and environmental issues. Evaluation includes in-class activities, presentation assignment, final project, and a final exam.​​ Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.course_name: Aviation Communication Skills – Crew Resource Management
courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: ​This course is the foundation for effective communication skills for an aviation environment. It includes the following topics: the fundamentals of interpersonal communication, effective listening and questioning skills, the effect that diversity has on communications, the challenges of communication in aviation operations workplace, presentation skills so that your message is understood and remembered and maximizing the impact of meetings. Learners will develop the written and oral communication skills to enable them to become effective communicators in the working environment. Evaluation includes a presentation and examination.​ Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: ​This course focuses on developing the skills of researching, organizing, and sequencing to produce a variety of internal and external correspondences used in an aviation environment. Students will learn how to create business letters, short and long reports, NOTAMs/incident reports and apply manual formatting. Evaluation includes quizzes, a letter, and a report examination.​ Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: ​This course provides students with the specific skills and techniques needed to become successful and effective learners. These fundamental concepts, behaviors, and competencies are useful not only in a learning environment but can also be applied in the workplace environment. Evaluation includes a Student Success assignment and examination.​ Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: ​This course is designed to meet the knowledge requirements of a Private Pilot Permit. The course includes topics such as Canadian Aviation Regulations, aerodynamics, theory of flight, weather, aircraft engine and systems, flight instruments, navigation, radio and electronic theory, flight operations and licensing requirements. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: This course provides the experience requirements to qualify for a Private Pilot Licence (Fixed Wing). It includes solo and dual flight instruction and practice. Local, cross country and instrument flying is also included. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: This course will cover in detail the effects of weather on general aviation and prepare the student for the private pilot meteorological exam. Topics will include the Earth's atmosphere, altimetry, stability and instability, weather systems, thunderstorms, and weather maps and other aviation related meteorological products. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: AVFO 1035 and AVFO 1145
courses.course_overview_raw: This course is designed to meet the knowledge requirements of a Private Pilot License. It is the primary ground school for the Private Pilot License and includes lessons on Canadian Aviation Regulations, aerodynamics, theory of flight, weather, aircraft engine and systems, flight instruments, navigation, radio and electronic theory, human factors, flight operations and licensing requirements. Prerequisite(s): AVFO 1035 and AVFO 1145

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: This course is designed to meet the knowledge requirements for a Private Pilot Licence. Lessons are held before and after flights and are used to prepare for flight and review flight outcomes. Includes completion of a Student Pilot Permit and radio licence. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.course_name: Air Navigation and Air Traffic Services
courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: This introductory course focuses on the fundamentals of air navigation and air traffic services and procedures. This is accomplished by introducing the history and development of Air Traffic Control (ATC), terminology, classifications, rules, procedures, methods of navigation, functions, responsibilities, and roles of all of the players in the world of Air Traffic Control. Evaluation includes two exams. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: ​This course covers the principles of leading and managing people in an aviation environment. Topics will include motivation strategies, understanding human behavior, basic airline/airport organization and structure, function of a leader in an aviation operation, the role and responsibilities of first line leaders and ethics in the workplace. Students participate in classroom activities and have opportunities for active learning. Evaluation includes a case study, presentation and examination.​ Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: This course will develop understanding of the relationship of effective safety programs and successful aviation operations with a focus on accident prevention and the associated concepts of risk management. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.course_name: Community and Public Relations for Aviation
courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: This course provides an introduction to public relations techniques and strategies in an aviation environment. Topics to be included are: issue management, media relations, and speaking to the media. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: ​This course consists of four modules of learning which will provide students with working knowledge of dangerous goods recognition, aircraft de-/anti-icing procedures, air cargo processing in compliance with the Transport Canada and Transportation Safety Administration (TSA) regulations, and ramp safety practices. The course emphasizes the responsibilities of flight crew in understanding how ground operations directly affect aircraft integrity, regulatory compliance, and overall flight safety.​ Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: Lessons in this course include instruction to prepare the applicant for the flight test aeroplane (TP2655E) Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: AVFO 2030
courses.course_overview_raw: This course will cover in detail the effects of weather on flying and airport operations. Topics will include weather office operational concepts, runway snow clearance, aircraft de-icing and severe weather effects on airport operations. Prerequisite(s): AVFO 2030

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: The focus of this course is a comprehensive study of the applicable security regulations in the Canadian Aeronautics Act (Aerodrome and Air Carrier measures) and its implications in designing and managing air carrier and airport security systems. The following topics will include access control, screening techniques, investigative procedures, customs and immigration procedures, limitations of authority and legal responsibilities. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: This course will provide an introduction to the maintenance systems and procedures applied to aircraft. The student will learn the roles of aircraft maintenance engineers, Approved Maintenance Organizations (AMOs) and Transport Canada in maintaining and certifying aircraft. Lessons include: practical sessions performing permitted elementary maintenance on an aircraft. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: This course prepares the student to respond to situations that may occur while flying over mountain, water and wilderness terrain. Topics will include water ditching and techniques to survive in the wilderness. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.course_name: Crew Resource Management 1: Human Factors for Pilots
courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: The focus of the course is to develop an understanding of human factors and its impact on decision-making, critical thinking, task performance, and accident prevention in an airline environment. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: AVFO 2060 and AVFO 2102 and AVFO 2132
courses.course_overview_raw: This course will focus on the airmanship in relation to basic aerodynamics, flight characteristics, engines, systems, and flight instruments for rotary-wing/helicopters. Emphasis is placed on applying aerodynamic theory to actual flight situations as well as engine and instrument operation during flight. Prerequisite(s): AVFO 2060 and AVFO 2102 and AVFO 2132

courses.prerequisite_raw: AIRC 1008 and AIRC 2126 and AVFO 2060 and AVFO 2165 and AVFO 3116
courses.course_overview_raw: This course will introduce Canadian Aviation Regulations to students, with emphasis on those regulations applying to commercial flight and rotary-wing flight. Review of Canadian airspace divisions and characteristics will be completed as they pertain to rotary-wing operations. Specific commercial training requirements and flight duty times will be covered, including a review of pilot decision-making models in the operations of commercial rotary-wing/helicopter operations. Prerequisite(s): AIRC 1008 and AIRC 2126 and AVFO 2060 and AVFO 2165 and AVFO 3116

courses.prerequisite_raw: AIRC 1005 and AVFO 2060 and AVFO 3116
courses.course_overview_raw: This course will teach students to prepare complete commercial flight plans, including charts, logs, and ICAO flight plans. In addition, students will review meteorological theory and integrate current and forecasted weather data into flight plans, to meet commercial flight test exam standards. This course will combine instruction and practical application of skills in preparing complete flight planning packages. Prerequisite(s): AIRC 1005 and AVFO 2060 and AVFO 3116

courses.prerequisite_raw: AVFO 2045 and AVFO 2060
courses.course_overview_raw: This course will focus on the early rotary-wing/helicopter flight lessons. Students will practice assisted take offs and landings and learn the basics of airspeed control, power changes, climbing, descending and turning. There will be an introduction of circuit procedures, approaching and departing transitions, autorotation entry/landing, and hydraulics off landings. The student will practice hovering and sloping ground exercises. Prerequisite(s): AVFO 2045 and AVFO 2060

courses.prerequisite_raw: AVFO 3205
courses.course_overview_raw: In this course, students will build proficiency in all basic flight exercises in preparation for the first rotary-wing solo flight. Prerequisite(s): AVFO 3205

courses.prerequisite_raw: AVFO 3210
courses.course_overview_raw: This course builds on the rotary-wing flight training, with a focus on rotary-wing exercise proficiency, including but not limited to skills supporting the basic concepts of navigation, and emergencies. By the end of the course, students will have accumulated up to 50 hours of rotary-wing flight experience, including solo cross country flights and solo proficiency planning flights. Prerequisite(s): AVFO 3210

courses.prerequisite_raw: AVFO 4050
courses.course_overview_raw: This course builds on exercise proficiency and develops skills with the advanced concepts of sloping ground, confined areas, vortex ring, and maximum weight. This course also builds necessary proficiency to qualify students for their written / flight exams and licensing. Prerequisite(s): AVFO 4050

courses.prerequisite_raw: AVFO 4150
courses.course_overview_raw: This course focuses on flight performance proficiency to prepare for the Transport Canada Exam. Students will be introduced to post-flight exam topics to complete their required training hours. The extent that these topics will be presented depends on the students overall progress toward their flight exam and the successful completion of their flight exam. Prerequisite(s): AVFO 4150

courses.prerequisite_raw: AVFO 3045 and AVFO 3136 and AVFO 3165 and AVFO 3175 and AVFO 3185 and AVFO 4155
courses.course_overview_raw: This course includes the necessary hours of flight training to complete practical exams, and preparation for the Transport Canada Commercial Helicopter exam (both written and practical). Prerequisite(s): AVFO 3045 and AVFO 3136 and AVFO 3165 and AVFO 3175 and AVFO 3185 and AVFO 4155

courses.prerequisite_raw: AIRC 1001
courses.course_overview_raw: This course will develop an understanding of the critical elements of an effective job search strategy including writing a cover letter and resume. Practical application will include mock interviews. Prerequisite(s): AIRC 1001

admission.raw: We strongly recommend applicants complete the Transport Canada Category 1 Medical Examination first, as that process takes the longest time to process. Scheduled intakes April or May each year. Application processing Applications are accepted from June 1st* to December 15th.* *or next business day We recommend that you apply early . All supporting documents must be submitted by the application deadline. Entrance requirements Competitive Entry: Two-step process Preference will be given to applicants with: Academic grades above the minimum Requirements completed within the last five years Related experience Additional post-secondary academic courses Applicants with preferred entrance requirements are to submit transcripts and supporting documentation with their online application. Step 1: Meet the following entrance requirements English language proficiency: one of the following: Category 2 – English Studies 12 (67%) or equivalent or BCIT English Trades Entry Assessment Math: one of the following: Pre-Calculus 11 (50%) or Foundations of Math 11 (50%) or Workplace Math 11 (60%) or Other acceptable BC and Yukon courses or BCIT Math Trades Entry Assessment BCIT Abstract Reasoning Trades Entry Assessment BCIT Mechanical Reasoning Trades Entry Assessment Transport Canada Category One Aviation Medical Complete the following form for submission with your online application: Mandatory Applicant Questionnaire [PDF] : This form will be used with other entrance requirements in the competitive selection for the program. Read more about how to meet BCIT’s entrance requirements Step 2: Requirements for selected applicants All complete applications will be reviewed by the program and shortlisted applicants will be required to complete the following: Multiple Mini Interview Process (MMI) During this process, applicants will be assessed for their suitability for this profession. Final selection into the program will be based on the results of the MMI assessment. Note : Interviews are usually held the third week of January. In order to prepare for their interview, applicants are advised to conduct their own research on the profession. Admission is competitive and will be offered to the most qualified applicants. Recommended for success It is strongly recommended that all applicants attend an Airline and Flight Operation Information Session prior to applying for this program. A driver's licence valid in BC is an asset. A good understanding of MS Office (Word, Excel and PowerPoint) computer software is highly recommended. Applicants should also take a familiarization flight at any flying school that offers them. Validation of previous Private Pilot Licence (PPL) flying time Candidates that hold a full or partial Private Pilot Licence (PPL) or full Recreational Pilot Permit (RPP) may be eligible for an exemption from a portion of their flying time. Exemptions from flying time are subject to the following conditions: You may apply for credit if you have a full and valid PPL, a full RPP, or if you have completed a PPL flight or written test. Your exemption will be determined for flight training and licensing courses in Term 1 and 2 only. If granted credit, you will still need to complete a minimum of 20 hours of flight training and a mock flight test with a designated flight test examiner The maximum flying time you can be credited is 45 hours.
